title: Live Mixing 起手參考：聽到問題先動手
intended_use: GTA live FOH soundcheck aid; Yamaha CL/QL, DiGiCo parameter translation required; not a downloadable console scene
methodology: 打開原文網頁／PDF，查核相關段落，而非只憑 search snippets；source findings 保留專家實際講法，同卡片綜合範圍分開。
每張卡列多來源，但部分第二來源只支持 mic placement／live safety／一般 dynamics，唔代表兩位專家逐一背書每個數字。
所有卡片數值（包括 Q、gain、HPF slope、attack/release range）一律標 editorial_synthesis；只有 source_findings 內明列嘅數字先係來源直接例子。
唔捏造不存在嘅專家設定；非公開書籍／付費課冇讀到就唔引用，亦唔假借 Dave Rat／Big Mick 等人背書。
選材以穩健低 GR 同 live GBF 為先；錄音室經驗只轉用原則，不直接複製 makeup／room-heavy 壓法。
global_defaults: 所有 EQ bands 及 HPF 默认 disabled，先 flat 聽 source；唔好一鍵加晒卡片所有 cut/boost。
數字係搜尋／調整區間：揀一個 frequency／Q 試，而唔係對成個範圍全部 cut。gain 範圍係有需要時可試嘅量，0 dB/bypass 永遠有效。
q 只適用 bell；shelf/LPF 的 q=null；無通用固定 feedback notch frequency。
comp 原則上先 bypass；先校 gain 及 fader balance，再視需要用 GR 調 threshold。mode=optional 亦唔代表自動啟用。
target_gr_db 表示較大聲有效段嘅典型 peak GR，不是全程平均值，更唔係安全 limiter 目標。
range_db 是 gate/expander 關閉時衰減正數；不是 compressor ratio。
live_safety: 先安排 mic／speaker 位置、正確 polar null、stage volume、system EQ 同 headroom。channel EQ 無法救錯誤 coverage／太遠距離。
壓縮本身唔係 feedback 必然來源；問題多係 makeup、提高 fader／平均增益、spill。唔用 compressor 當 feedback suppressor。
wedge 路徑要獨立判斷：FOH comp／EQ 未必適合 monitor，亦要 check aux tap pre/post-EQ/dynamics/fader。pre-fader 不等於 pre-dynamics。
CL/QL／DiGiCo 可 split input 但可能共享 head amp；保護 monitor gain、check trim／gain compensation，唔隨意改 shared preamp。
唔好將 monitor 輸出 EQ 當 channel 音色 EQ；先調系統，再細修聲源。反饋點隨咪位／人數／場地變，不預載通用 notch。
測試低音量起步；唔刻意製造持續 loud feedback，唔以耳朵近距離查找；足夠 loudness 就停，保留 show headroom。
先停／mute 再插拔可能有 pop 嘅線／phantom；保護人耳同 PA。
console_translation: 用 GR meter 而非抄 threshold dBFS；preamp、detector calibration、峰值/RMS、comp model 都影響結果。
soft/medium/hard 係聽感選擇，唔宣稱 Yamaha 數字 knee 同 DiGiCo 某 dB knee 等價；按實際 console manual 對照。
相同 attack/release 毫秒未必同聲：envelope/detector/time-constant 定義不同。Yamaha gate Decay 可對照 release 用途，但要聽。
唔用 Q=1／slope 等同保證跨 desk 響應一致；特殊 shelf／dynamic EQ 更要現場確認。
本稿未製作／驗證 Yamaha 或 DiGiCo scene preset，亦唔宣稱廠方認證。

disagreements.detail: SOS 建議約10 ms、50–100 ms、≤約5 dB peak GR；Yamaha 舊 live 教材建議最快 attack、約40 ms release、可到10 dB。係目的／時代／聲源／模型有差，唔係一個必然啱。呢份卡片揀較保守 GR，保留 transient 同 monitor 穩定性。

disagreements.topic: Drum fast attack 定 slow attack
disagreements.detail: 控制不均勻 peaks 可用快 attack；保留 stick/punch 可用慢 attack，Yamaha 例子到50–70 ms／300 ms。卡片較中庸；唔將 fast attack 一律叫更 punch。
BTM 某 mix bass HPF60 Hz、kick50 Hz；SOS mixing 文章亦提 domestic playback 可刪50 Hz 以下。live full-range、5-string low B唔可照抄；按演奏音域／PA 選25–40 Hz起步，必要才提高。
好多習慣會刪 bottom body 或 gate 全鼓；Jon Burton 特別保留有用 bottom body、很少 gate top。呢份默認 top 不 gate、bottom optional。
頻率表幫你聽／搵問題，唔係要求每個 band 都處理。良好 source/placement 可能完全唔需要 EQ/comp。
studio vocal 壓法唔可以原封不動用落 distant choir；live 優先 mic geometry、少開咪、唔送 distant choir mics 返 wedges。

coverage_limits: 包含28張 instrument/bus 卡片；每張數值係編者綜合，不應包裝成多位專家一致認證。
未加入 erhu／guzheng／dizi 數值：今次未取得足夠可信、互相印證嘅 live EQ/comp 起手證據；唔直接套 violin／guitar／flute 冒充專業民族樂器 preset。
sources 內 DPA 支持 mic placement／音色取捨，不提供本稿壓縮數字；strings／ride／choral 數值證據較薄，以 bypass 優先。
資料頁跨年代，係專家技術原則研究，不係2026最新 desk firmware 功能審核。

sos-live-drums.title: Engineering Drums Live: Part Two
sos-live-drums.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: Jon Burton: external kick low-mid cut 200–400 Hz, optional click 2–5 kHz; rarely adds bass to external mic.
Gate attenuation 20–30 dB; uses key filtering and may link two kick gates; rarely gates snare top; bottom gate may be keyed from top.
Hi-hat/tom HPF: raise until audible thinning then back down. Bottom snare need not have all body filtered out.
Heavy live drum-group compression raises spill; overheads may be excluded; PA capability takes priority over desired bass.

sos-essentials.title: Mixing Essentials
sos-essentials.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-essentials.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: Voice: boxy 200–400 Hz, nasal 800–1500 Hz, penetrating 2–4 kHz, airy 7–12 kHz.
Kick weight 70–100 Hz, click 3–5 kHz; snare definition 1–3 kHz; cymbal sizzle 5–12 kHz.
Bass: deep 50–100 Hz, character 200–400 Hz, hard 1–2 kHz, fret noise 2–7 kHz.
Acoustic: boom 80–150 Hz, box 150–300 Hz, hardness 800–1500 Hz, presence 2.5–4 kHz, scratch 4–8 kHz. These are listening regions, not instructions to cut everything.

sos-vocal.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: Published vocal example: ratio 2–4:1, attack around 10 ms, release 50–100 ms, no more than about 5 dB peak GR for a natural result.

sos-drums-comp.title: Drum Compression
sos-drums-comp.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-drums-comp.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: One consistency-control example uses 5:1, fast attack, medium release and up to 4–5 dB GR; attack/release changes can instead shape punch.

sos-acoustic.title: Processing Acoustic Guitars
sos-acoustic.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-acoustic.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: In a busy arrangement, cut below 100 Hz; gentle 2:1 compression to catch peaks; exposed guitar generally needs subtler processing.
Change mic position before drastic EQ. The article’s −15 dB threshold is example-specific, not portable.

sos-jazz.title: Session Notes: Selwyn Jazz Part 2
sos-jazz.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-jazz.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: Mike Senior session: bass 2–4 dB GR, roughly 25 ms attack / 80 ms release; piano only 2–3 dB GR.
A 5:1 trombone setting is a particular session solution, not a universal horn preset.

sos-brass.title: Recording Brass & Reeds
sos-brass.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-brass.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: Mild compression can tame brass/reed peaks; fairly fast attack/release suggested but preserve bite. Excessive compression emphasises sax mechanical noises.
With appropriate microphone choice/placement, little EQ may be needed.

sos-strings.title: Recording Strings
sos-strings.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-strings.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: String sections usually need little processing; if necessary, gently compress louder peaks. Makeup on distant mics emphasises room/noise.

shure-choir.title: Of Mics and Monitors: Live Sound Reinforcement Tips for Choirs
shure-choir.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: Minimum microphones, thoughtful placement, stage level and pattern orientation before EQ; adding open mics reduces available GBF.
Advises against sending distant choir microphones into choir wedges. The 3:1 rule is a useful spill/interference guideline, not a guarantee of phase coherence.

yamaha-gate.title: How to Use a Noise Gate
findings: Drums need fast opening, lower toms longer decay. Backing vocal gating can use slower opening and only 10–15 dB attenuation.
Avoid gates on wide-dynamic-range singers, clean DI sources and long-sustain guitar.

yamaha-comp.title: How to Use a Compressor
findings: Use compression only as needed live; monitor processing can affect the singer’s performance and excessive compression/makeup can reduce practical GBF.

yamaha-tech.title: For Audio Techs: Compression
yamaha-tech.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: A contrasting live teaching recipe: lead 2:1 / backing 3–4:1, fastest attack, around 40 ms release, potentially 1–10 dB GR; drums 4:1, 50–70 ms attack, around 300 ms release.
Its suggestion to replace GR with equivalent makeup gain is NOT adopted as a live safety rule here.

btm-guitar.title: Mixing Electric Guitars
findings: Chris Huff live guitar: HPF 100–200 Hz, LPF 6–10 kHz, body 200–600 Hz; inspect 1–6 kHz for tone/harshness.
Guitar role and amp mic placement matter; compression only for excessive level range.

btm-keys.title: Keyboard Mixing
findings: Brian Gowing live piano patch: low roll-off 100–150 Hz with bass present, inspect mud near 250 Hz, optional air 10–16 kHz, space in 1–3 kHz.
Usually avoids extra dynamics because patches may already have processing. Article frequency table has errors and is NOT used here.

btm-bass.title: The Foundation of the Perfect Mix
findings: Derek Sexsmith live example divides kick near 50 Hz and bass 80–100 Hz; bass HPF near 60 Hz, clarity 1–1.5 kHz.
This is an arrangement-specific alternative, NOT suitable automatically for preserving 5-string low B. Its fast-attack/punch wording is not adopted as a universal rule.

sos-pads.title: Creating & Using Synth Pad Sounds
sos-pads.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-pads.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: A pad supporting an arrangement may be high-passed at 200 Hz to avoid low-mid mud. This does not apply automatically to bass synth.

sos-bus.title: Pro Tools: Bus & Group Compression
sos-bus.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
sos-bus.context: studio/mixing principles; adapted cautiously for live use
findings: Bus compression creates interdependence between sources; backing-vocal bus can blend a stack, independent channel compressors control individual singers. Stereo linking changes image behaviour.

dpa-piano.title: How to mic piano
dpa-piano.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: For stage/pit piano, closer directional mic placement inside the instrument and shorter/closed lid can improve isolation; distant natural pickup is a different goal.

dpa-violin.title: How to mic violin
dpa-violin.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: Close-mounted violin position balances soundboard and string bite; it may sound harsh but offers stage separation. Position before EQ.

dpa-cello.title: How to mic cello
dpa-cello.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: Close-mic placement and proximity effect influence captured cello body; preserve natural tone before adding processing.

dpa-saxophone.title: How to mic saxophone
dpa-saxophone.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: Sax radiates from tone holes as well as bell; capture a balanced mixture rather than assuming the bell alone is the instrument.

dpa-acoustic-guitar.title: How to mic acoustic-guitar
dpa-acoustic-guitar.verification_method: HTTP 200; original article saved; relevant passages inspected
findings: Start between fretboard and sound hole; microphone position/proximity change low-end balance.

shure-processors.title: Selection and Operation of Audio Signal Processors
findings: Speech-intelligibility example: 125 Hz low cut, 6 dB/oct; publication also gives a 4 kHz high cut. This narrow-band system example is not automatically adopted for modern full-range MC sound.
Gain structure/headroom and microphone/loudspeaker geometry are fundamental; EQ cannot fix arbitrary acoustic limits.
